Subject: Re: Clarify SOC2 evidence cadence + pen test language for MSA/Order Form

Tom — thanks, and thanks for the list. Quick read-through below and a proposed operational approach so NovaMed has predictable coverage without a broad, open-ended inspection right.

Proposal summary (high level):
- SOC 2: Redwood will provide an annual SOC 2 Type II report and quarterly snapshot artifacts (control evidence index + aggregated system logs for the scope) on a 90-day cadence. Snapshots are scoped to in-scope systems defined in the Order Form.
- Pen test: Customer provides 30 calendar days’ notice for a non-production penetration test. Redwood will provide ephemeral staging credentials and an allowlist window for up to 72 hours. Allowed tooling must be disclosed in advance and destructive testing is disallowed (no data exfiltration, no production scope).
- Audit rights: Replace unlimited "inspection" language with a bounded, sampled-access clause: limited to (a) review of artifacts, (b) on-site technical interviews by mutual agreement, and (c) ephemeral access to scoped staging systems for scheduled pen tests only. All access is subject to Redwood’s evidence workflow and an execution SOW that limits frequency and systems sampled.

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ve attached our draft security exhibit for redline (Redwood_Security_Exhibit_Draft_v1.docx). Please review and mark any absolute must-haves for NovaMed counsel.
2) Karthik — can you propose clean contract language for the bounded inspection clause and the pen test carveouts?
3) Laura — can you provide the operational pen-test checklist we require (IP allowlist, ephemeral creds, how we deliver logs/artifacts)?

If it helps, happy to schedule a 30-min working call tomorrow 11am PT.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Security & Assurance 
Redwood Inference

Team — looping in legal commentary for the draft. High-level legal asks and proposed contract text fragments below. I wanted to get these to you before we send anything back to NovaMed counsel.

Key legal positions (draft form):
1) Scoped inspection: "Customer inspection rights are limited to review of written artifacts and scheduled, time-boxed technical sessions for sampled systems expressly identified in the Order Form. Any on-site inspection requires 30 days advance notice and mutual agreement of scope and personnel."

2) Pen-test carveout: "Customer may perform permitted security testing only against non-production environments identified in the Order Form. Customer must provide a test plan, list of tools, and a minimum 30-day notice. Redwood will provide ephemeral credentials and an IP allowlist window not to exceed 72 hours. Tests that could cause destructive behavior or access customer data are expressly prohibited."

3) Evidence delivery and confidentiality: "Redwood will provide SOC 2 reports and quarterly evidence snapshots via a secure link. All evidence is provided under NDA and may contain Redwood confidential material; Customer shall not disclose or use evidence except for compliance review."

Operational notes for Laura (please confirm):
- Minimum artifact set for a quarterly snapshot: control mapping index (CSV), aggregate auth logs (last 90 days), system config manifest, and change-control tickets for the period.
- For pen-test artifacts: test results summary, vuln scan output, and redacted logs showing exploit traces; raw forensic-level logs may be provided under a separate request and only for the sampled systems.

Marissa — FYI this likely changes the Order Form language around "unfettered inspection" and should be surfaced to sales as a standard fallback.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel

Tom — thanks for the questions and for reviewing Soojin's draft. From a technical ops perspective, here’s the acceptance criteria and practical runbook we’ll use if NovaMed signs the proposed language. Sharing so procurement/legal know exactly what we need operationally.

Pen test operations (practical checklist):
- Notice: 30 calendar days prior with a test plan and approved tool list.
- Environment: tests must run against Redwood-managed staging environment(s) that mirror in-scope services. Production services are out of scope.
- Access: ephemeral credentials issued via our secrets service; access window is 1–72 hours depending on test class.
- IP allowlist: Customer must provide source IP ranges at least 7 days before window for firewall allowlist.
- Prohibited activity: no data exfiltration, no escalation attempts into tenant-managed customer data, no destructive payloads.

Artifacts we provide after a test:
- Executive summary and remediation timeline (7 business days)
- Vulnerability report/scores and remediation notes
- Redacted application and auth logs supporting findings (90-day retention)

SOC2 / evidence snapshots:
- Annual SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) + quarterly snapshot package (control index CSV, aggregated auth logs for the quarter, change-control manifest).
- Snapshots delivered via secure link; retention of snapshots: 90 days by default, archival on request under an additional agreement.

I’m attaching a concise ops checklist (pen-test-ops-checklist.xlsx) that maps each contractual clause to the runbook step. Once legal signs off on the three contract fragments Karthik proposed, we can attach the ops checklist as an appendix to the security exhibit. That should satisfy NovaMed’s need for operational certainty while limiting legal exposure from open-ended inspection clauses.

Happy to review the redline callouts on a short call — propose Wed 11am PT if that works.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
